reference: GNU coreutils uniq, invoked by system Bash with /usr/bin:/bin in PATH under C locale and UTC; the identical scripts run under bash-os with an empty PATH, so uniq resolves to the compiled builtin. Parity expectations come from the independent GNU execution, with each reference status checked against expected_status.
coverage: Default adjacent-record filtering, blank records, nonadjacent repeats, and unterminated final input.
Count, repeated-only, and singleton-only output modes.
Field and character skips, including differing whitespace after a skipped field.
Bounded comparison lengths, including zero compared characters.
All-lines-from-duplicate-groups selection and its separator methods.
Group output with separate, prepend, append, and both separators.
NUL-delimited records containing embedded newlines and an unterminated final record.
Relative input and output operands, including replacement of an existing output file.
Invalid numeric option argument status and diagnostic presence.
Bash builtin type and help metadata contract.
exclusions: Version text and exact diagnostic wording are not compared.
A PTY-driven check for record delivery before stdin reaches EOF is deferred because this runner only supplies captured streams.
Unlisted GNU options and extreme-size/resource behavior are outside this compact suite.

cases.purpose: Check default suppression of adjacent duplicates while retaining blank records, a later nonadjacent repeat, and a final record without an input newline.
Compare count formatting and the -d/-u run selectors over mixed singleton and repeated groups.
cases.script:
input=$'oak
oak
pine
fir
fir
fir
'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq -c; printf '%s
' '-- repeated --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq -d; printf '%s
' '-- singletons --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq -u

cases.purpose: Exercise -f and -s comparison offsets. The first input deliberately varies whitespace after the skipped field to expose field-boundary handling differences.
cases.script:
printf 'x   key
y key
z other
' | uniq --skip-fields=1; printf '%s
' '-- skip characters --'; printf 'xapple
yapple
zberry
qberry
' | uniq -s 1

cases.purpose: Check -w comparison prefixes and the zero-character boundary, where every record has an empty comparison key.
cases.script:
printf 'ab-one
ab-two
ac-one
ac-two
' | uniq --check-chars=2; printf '%s
' '-- zero compared characters --'; printf 'x
y
z
' | uniq -w 0

cases.purpose: Verify case-insensitive grouping in the runner's C locale and preservation of each group's first spelling.
Compare duplicate-group selection without separators, with separate separators, and with a blank line prepended to every selected group.
cases.script:
input=$'a
a
b
c
c
c
d
d
'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq -D; printf '%s
' '-- separate --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq --all-repeated=separate; printf '%s
' '-- prepend --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq --all-repeated=prepend

cases.purpose: Check that --group emits all groups and applies separate, prepend, append, and both separator policies at group boundaries.
cases.script:
input=$'a
a
b
c
c
'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq --group=separate; printf '%s
' '-- prepend --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq --group=prepend; printf '%s
' '-- append --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq --group=append; printf '%s
' '-- both --'; printf '%s' "$input" | uniq --group=both

cases.purpose: Verify NUL record framing with embedded newlines and a final record missing its delimiter.
Read and write only relative fixture files; verify that the output operand replaces stale contents with deduplicated records.
cases.script:
printf 'pear
pear
plum' > input.txt; printf 'stale output
' > output.txt; uniq input.txt output.txt

cases.purpose: Check GNU uniq's failure status for a negative skip-field count and require a diagnostic without pinning localized wording.
Contract check that uniq is registered as a Bash builtin and its help entry is available; expected output is the documented Bash type classification.
cases.script:
trap 'rm -f discard.out' EXIT
[[ $(type -t uniq) == builtin ]] || exit 44; help uniq >discard.out || exit 45; printf 'builtin\n'

cases.purpose: Deferred check of stream delivery while input remains open after complete records.
Empty input emits nothing; missing input returns failure and a diagnostic.
